description: We are three software people and a data scientist building Mars mapping software! Team formed in-person on 11/13, not looking to accept additional members remotely at present.
summary: We built a HUD app to map an area, and either generate a simulation to allow astronauts to walk through the area while planning or training for a mission, or run as an AR navigation tool when walking through the actual area. Our tool is primarily focused on astronaut safety, and provides mapping information and live alerts for local hazards, including weather, radiation, and temperature extremes.
details:
Our project is a Unity application, which uses a Python-based backend to access publicly-available NASA data to build its simulation. The application allows the user to place waypoints using a minimap of the wider area, then tracks their progress through the area, while providing alerts about local hazards.

We use a modified A* search for navigation, adding terms to penalize steep slopes, and use Tobler's Hiking Function to estimate walking time, slowed down to account for the difficulty of moving in a spacesuit. The frontend UI is built using standard Unity C# scripting. We used Meta's VR SDK to get our application running on a VR headset.

We envision this project serving as a mission planning aid in simulation mode allowing astronauts to do a virtual walkthrough of any environment, and then as a live navigation HUD during a mission.

Our project requires no live input from an astronaut during a mission, allowing the astronaut to focus on maneuvering through the environment and performing tasks within the environment, while providing them information they can use to navigate and avoid hazards.
